source.title: Causal Activation Steering via Sparse Mediation
source.authors: Toan Doan; Uyen Le; T. Nguyen

record.tranche_reason: The study uses neuron dimensions as units for sparse activation steering and reports steering-method results, but does not test the listed audit, explanation, attribution-graph, or explanation-scoring claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports measurements of how steering-induced activation changes concentrate across neuron dimensions; these are recorded below as findings not covered by a claim version. Its behavioral steering scores assess CAS-BiPO performance, not whether neurons have one or more identifiable jobs, so they are omitted.
record.test_reason: A steering-method paper (CAS-BiPO). It learns a sparse mask over layer-15 residual-stream dimensions and reports its own method's steering and concentration results. It never audits neuron jobs, explains neurons from activating examples, scores explanations by simulation, builds attribution graphs, or examines InceptionV1. Its 'neurons' are residual-stream basis dimensions, not MLP neurons, and no unit is assigned a job. No result bears on V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that learned sparse masks concentrate steering effects, which they say validates a 'sparse mediation hypothesis'. They also conclude that CAS-BiPO keeps 97–100% of dense BiPO effectiveness using 10–30% of dimensions, and offers interpretable, controllable edits. They note that evaluation is limited to 7B models, so scaling is unvalidated.
record.recipe_differences: Extends BiPO with a learned sparse mask and adaptive sparsity regularization; it is a steering intervention study, not a neuron-explanation audit.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies target sparsity, behavior, model, and judge. Its appendix reports judge-dependent behavioral scores and attack-success rates; these do not test the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama-2-7b-chat (power-seeking, layer 15, τ=0.8), a learned mask over 26.7% of residual-stream dimensions captured 94.3% of layer-16 steering-induced activation change, vs about 51–53% for a same-size random subset. 49 of the top 50 changed dimensions fell inside the mask.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering-induced activation changes concentrate in a learned sparse subset of residual-stream dimensions. This is a sparse-mediation result, not a neuron-job audit.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL) 2026
record.problems: The paper states that evaluations focus on mid-sized models and curated benchmarks with LLM judges, that scaling to larger models remains unvalidated, and that cross-domain transfer is not explored. The neuron-dimension analysis is reported for one behavior, model, and layer.
record.rows_left_out: Behavioral steering effectiveness results in Table 1 and Appendix B, sparsity-control ablations in Table 3, and judge-robustness results in Table 4 were left out because they evaluate CAS-BiPO behavior control, not neuron-job interpretability or the listed explanation claims.

untested.parts: All: audit shares in other dense or MoE models and at scale.
All: InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, recursive generalization.
All: architecture, regularization and tool effects on the share of interpretable neurons.
All: neuron-based attribution graphs vs replacement models.
All: explanations from activating examples vs held-out firing prediction.
All: simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The 'neurons' here are hidden residual-stream dimensions (d=4096), not MLP neurons with poles. No semantic job is assigned to any unit. The concentration analysis covers one behaviour, one model and one layer. Random-baseline figures are internally inconsistent (51.2% vs 52.6%; 1.92×, 1.84×, 1.79×).

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B pole-job proportions and explanation testing on held-out activations.
Whether the audit shares generalize across models, architectures, or scales up to trillions of parameters.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose as its shared feature, and recursive generalization.
The proposed architecture, regularization, and tool effects, and the estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Attribution graphs, explaining model behavior with them, and comparisons with replacement models or reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit to activating examples predict where neurons fire on separate examples.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat-hf
rows.operation_detail: Measured the share of downstream steering-induced activation changes captured by the learned sparse mask.

conditions.value: 15; downstream activation changes measured at layer 16

rows.note: The paper describes this as 3.54× concentration efficiency compared with a uniform/dense baseline.
rows.check: This is the study's own method's result (mask capture of steering-induced change). It is not a neuron-interpretability measure. The 'observed' state has no version to be judged against.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat-hf
rows.operation_detail: Measured activation-change capture for a random subset of dimensions.

conditions.value: 15; downstream activation changes measured at layer 16

rows.note: The authors describe this random baseline as proportional to its size.
rows.check: Random-subset control for the method. 'Partial' is meaningless with no version. The value is inconsistent across the paper: Table 2 gives 51.2% (1.92×), Figure 7 gives 52.6% (1.79×), and the text gives 1.84× for sparse vs random.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat-hf
rows.operation_detail: Reported concentration efficiency for the learned sparse mask.

conditions.value: 15; downstream activation changes measured at layer 16

rows.measure: Capture percentage divided by subset size percentage
rows.note: The paper also gives differing random-selection efficiency figures in different passages; this row records the learned-mask value from Table 2.
rows.check: Derived ratio of R1 (94.3/26.7). It restates R1 rather than adding a finding.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat-hf
rows.operation_detail: Compared median activation changes for masked and unmasked dimensions.

conditions.value: 15; downstream activation changes measured at layer 16

rows.measure: Median activation change in masked dimensions relative to other positions
rows.note: This measures activation-change magnitude, not whether a dimension has a single named job.
rows.check: Activation-change magnitude in masked vs unmasked residual dimensions. The comparison group is inconsistent: Section 5.2 says 'other positions', while Appendix D.1 says 'random selections' (Figure 7a: 0.0381 vs 0.0177/0.0174).

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat-hf
rows.operation_detail: Compared learned-mask membership with neuron activation-change importance rankings.

conditions.value: 15; downstream activation changes measured at layer 16

rows.measure: Overlap of top-ranked neurons with learned sparse support
rows.note: The paper reports 49/50 top neurons within the learned support and a point-biserial correlation of r = 0.450.
rows.check: Mask-membership vs activation-change ranking. This validates the method itself and is not a measure of neuron jobs.
